title: DOGE Accessed Social Security Data to Cross-Reference Voter Rolls, Violated Court Orders
description_short: DOGE Accessed Social Security Data to Cross-Reference Voter Rolls, Violated Court Orders
description_medium: A March 2025 agreement reportedly gave a political advocacy group access to Social Security voter data for efforts to find alleged voter fraud. A later court filing said DOGE staff had also shared sensitive Social Security data through an unauthorized server, potentially violating a temporary restraining order. The Social Security Administration acknowledged copying its live database, covering more than 300 million people, to a cloud server without independent security controls.
description_long: The agreement was signed on March 24, 2025, by DOGE staff embedded at the Social Security Administration and a political advocacy group whose stated purpose was to find voter fraud and overturn election results in certain states. The supplied account says a January 2026 court filing later disclosed that DOGE employees had also shared sensitive SSA information through an unauthorized Cloudflare server. The Social Security Administration acknowledged transferring a live copy of its database, covering more than 300 million people, to a cloud server without independent security controls. A temporary restraining order issued March 20 had barred DOGE from accessing SSA data, so the filing raised the possibility that the access and sharing violated the order; the description does not treat that as a final court finding. In December 2025, the Justice Department made two Hatch Act referrals to the U.S. Office of Special Counsel related to the conduct. The sequence links access to highly sensitive identity data with a group seeking to challenge election results. It documents reported agreements, security failures, and legal concerns, without claiming that the database established actual voter fraud or that every record was disclosed.

title: Deutsche Bank Laundered $10B+ in Russian Money — Trump's Primary Lender
description_short: Deutsche Bank Laundered $10B+ in Russian Money — Trump's Primary Lender
description_medium: In 2017, U.S. and U.K. regulators penalized Deutsche Bank over “mirror trades” that moved about $10 billion from Russia into Western markets. The bank was also a major lender to Donald Trump. Investigators sought Trump’s bank records, but the supplied source notes do not establish that Russian funds from the trades were connected to his loans or accounts.
description_long: Between 2011 and 2015, Deutsche Bank employees used so-called mirror trades to move Russian money into Western financial markets: Russian securities were bought in rubles and matching securities were sold in London for dollars. U.S. and British regulators later penalized the bank for anti-money-laundering failures connected to the scheme. New York’s Department of Financial Services imposed a $425 million penalty; the supplied synopsis reports total penalties of about $630 million across U.S. and U.K. regulators. At the same time, Deutsche Bank had been one of Donald Trump’s most important lenders, and a 2017 financial disclosure showed at least $130 million in liabilities to the bank. Congressional investigators sought Trump’s banking records to examine the relationship, and the bank initially resisted disclosure. The shared presence of Russian money laundering at the bank and Trump’s borrowing made the records a focus of scrutiny, but the supplied source notes explicitly do not establish that funds from the mirror trades were commingled with Trump loans or accounts. The event is therefore a documented regulatory case and lending relationship, alongside an unresolved question investigators pursued; it is not evidence that Trump participated in the bank’s scheme.

title: '90 Deals in 90 Days' Collapses: Only 2 Deals Reached by Deadline
description_short: '90 Deals in 90 Days' Collapses: Only 2 Deals Reached by Deadline
description_medium: During the 2025 tariff pause, White House adviser Peter Navarro promoted a goal of “90 deals in 90 days.” As the July 9 deadline approached, reporting described only limited U.K. and Vietnam arrangements; the supplied account notes China’s partial tariff reduction was sometimes counted as a third deal. The gap between the slogan and the agreements reached became a measure of the administration’s trade negotiations.
description_long: When Trump announced the 90-day tariff pause on April 9, 2025, White House trade adviser Peter Navarro boasted of '90 deals in 90 days,' and Trump himself claimed at his 100-day mark to have struck deals with '200 countries.' By the July 9 deadline, only two formal agreements had been reached — a partial framework with the United Kingdom and a preliminary deal with Vietnam. Trump then extended his own 'final' deadline to August 1, declaring 'no extensions will be granted,' only to extend it again. By July 9, 2025, CNN reported just three deals (UK, Vietnam, and China's partial 90-day tariff reduction), far short of the promised comprehensive restructuring of global trade. Foreign officials across 10 countries told Politico that negotiations were bogged down. The EU ultimately settled for a 15% tariff deal just days before August 1, with France immediately declaring it needed renegotiation.

title: Eric's Fake Blind Trust: Running the Business While Briefing Dad Quarterly
description_short: Eric's Fake Blind Trust: Running the Business While Briefing Dad Quarterly
description_medium: Donald Trump said his sons would manage his businesses while he was president. In March 2017, Eric Trump told Forbes he expected to give his father financial reports about the Trump Organization, probably quarterly. A later report found the trust allowed Trump to request distributions without public disclosure. Ethics critics said the arrangement did not create a meaningful separation from the family business.
description_long: When Donald Trump entered the White House in January 2017, he announced he was placing his businesses in a trust managed by his sons Eric and Donald Jr. — presenting this as ethical separation from his commercial interests. In March 2017, Eric Trump admitted to Forbes that he would provide his father with financial reports on the Trump Organization probably quarterly — directly contradicting the premise of the arrangement. A ProPublica investigation revealed that the trust document had been amended on February 10, 2017 to allow Trump to distribute net income or principal to Donald J. Trump at his request at any time, without public disclosure. Ethics watchdogs including Richard Painter, George W. Bush's former chief ethics lawyer, said the arrangement was malarkey. Eric and Donald Jr. continued to make major business deals — including expanding Trump hotels and golf properties — while their father was president, creating constant emoluments and conflict-of-interest concerns that were never adequately addressed.

title: RFK Jr. Declares Autism Epidemic Caused by Environmental Toxin, Distorts All Science
description_short: RFK Jr. Declares Autism Epidemic Caused by Environmental Toxin, Distorts All Science
description_medium: At an April 16, 2025, press conference, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. attributed rising autism prevalence to an environmental toxin and called autism preventable. A PBS fact check reported that autism researchers found the claim lacked evidence and omitted factors such as increased awareness that help explain rising diagnoses. The supplied synopsis also notes Kennedy’s claims about a retracted study and future costs.
description_long: On April 16, 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. held a press conference announcing new CDC autism prevalence data and declared autism a preventable epidemic caused by an unidentified environmental toxin. Kennedy contradicted established science on multiple fronts: he falsely stated that 75–85% of the observed increase in autism rates was real rather than attributable to broader diagnostic criteria, citing a retracted 2014 paper as support. FactCheck.org documented that Kennedy mischaracterized a 1970 Wisconsin study and in a later April 22 Fox News interview falsely claimed all the kids in Wisconsin were tested. Kennedy also falsely invoked a paper that had been retracted nearly two years prior, claiming autism costs would reach $1 trillion a year by 2035. Meanwhile, his agency eliminated NIOSH divisions studying environmental links to autism and canceled over $40 million in NIH autism research grants. ProPublica reported that Kennedy was simultaneously gutting the scientific infrastructure he claimed to need. His September deadline to identify the autism cause passed without results, as he later acknowledged his timeline was overly optimistic.
organization_tags: Department of Health and Human Services
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Marko Elez Given Admin Write-Access to $5.4T Federal Payment System
description_short: Marko Elez Given Admin Write-Access to $5.4T Federal Payment System
description_medium: On February 1, 2025, Treasury gave DOGE staffer Marko Elez read and write access to two Bureau of the Fiscal Service payment systems. Those systems processed $5.45 trillion in federal payments in fiscal year 2024. Although officials publicly described access as read-only, later Treasury filings said write permission had been granted by mistake and was not used to alter the payment database.
description_long: On February 1, 2025, the day after Treasury career official David Lebryk was placed on administrative leave for resisting DOGE, 25-year-old Marko Elez — a former SpaceX and X employee with no government or finance experience — was granted read and write access to the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's Payment Automation Manager (PAM) and Secure Payment System (SPS). These two systems processed $5.45 trillion in federal payments in fiscal year 2024, including Social Security checks, tax refunds, veterans' pay, and federal salaries. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent repeatedly told Congress and the press that DOGE's access was read-only. Treasury officials actually altered internal records to indicate Elez no longer had write access before senior IT staff stated it was rescinded. Reporting by Wired and Talking Points Memo confirmed Elez had already made extensive changes to the code base for the payment systems. His write access was not revoked until February 5, the day a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order. Five former Treasury Secretaries warned in a New York Times op-ed that DOGE had put America's payments system and the highly sensitive data within it to the risk of exposure, potentially to our adversaries.

title: OFCCP Ceases Affirmative Action Enforcement for Contractors
description_short: OFCCP Ceases Affirmative Action Enforcement for Contractors
description_medium: On January 21, 2025, an executive order revoking Executive Order 11246 led the Labor Department’s contractor compliance office to halt enforcement tied to that framework. Acting Labor Secretary Vincent Micone later directed the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to stop related investigations and reviews. The supplied account says the action also affected protections for LGBTQ+ workers at federal contractors.
description_long: On January 21, 2025, Trump's executive order revoking EO 11246 triggered an immediate halt to all affirmative action enforcement for federal contractors, a 60-year-old framework protecting millions of workers. The Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP), housed within the Department of Labor, was ordered to immediately cease and desist all investigative and enforcement activity tied to EO 11246. Acting Labor Secretary Vincent Micone issued a memo on January 24 directing the agency accordingly, administratively closing all approximately 2,000 pending compliance reviews that the Biden administration had scheduled for fiscal year 2025. Companies including Meta, Google, and Pfizer that had been slated for civil rights audits received formal closure notices. The Obama-era EO 13672 — which specifically prohibited federal contractors from discriminating on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity — was also revoked, eliminating protection for LGBTQ+ workers at companies doing business with the federal government, estimated to involve roughly 25 percent of the U.S. civilian workforce. Federal contractors were given a 90-day grace period until April 21, 2025 to wind down compliance with the old regulatory scheme. New contracts and grants were required to include certifications that recipients do not run DEI programs deemed discriminatory. Civil rights advocates called it the most significant rollback of workforce civil rights protections since the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
organization_tags: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs

title: 'China Virus' and Lab Leak Theory - Racist COVID Scapegoating
description_short: 'China Virus' and Lab Leak Theory - Racist COVID Scapegoating
description_medium: Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, Donald Trump repeatedly used terms such as “China virus” and “Kung flu” for the coronavirus and promoted a lab-leak explanation. Asian American organizations warned that stigmatizing language could encourage discrimination. The linked FBI report documents hate-crime statistics for 2020, but those statistics alone do not establish that specific attacks were caused by Trump’s remarks.
description_long: Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, Donald Trump consistently used racist language to describe the coronavirus, calling it the 'China virus,' 'Kung flu,' and 'Wuhan virus' while promoting conspiracy theories about its origin to deflect from his administration's failed pandemic response. Trump began using these terms in March 2020, deliberately choosing inflammatory language that Asian American organizations warned would increase hate crimes and discrimination against Asian communities. At rallies, Trump would pause for applause when using terms like 'Kung flu,' treating racist language as entertainment for his supporters. Trump also promoted the theory that COVID-19 escaped from a laboratory in Wuhan, China, using this claim to blame China for the pandemic while ignoring his own administration's slow response that contributed to hundreds of thousands of American deaths. While questions about COVID's origins remain legitimate scientific inquiry, Trump weaponized these discussions to scapegoat an entire ethnic group and distract from his administration's failures. His racist rhetoric coincided with a dramatic spike in hate crimes against Asian Americans, with many perpetrators explicitly citing Trump's language as justification for their attacks. Even as scientific consensus emerged that the virus likely emerged naturally, Trump continued promoting lab leak theories on Truth Social and at rallies, using them to maintain anger against China and Asian Americans generally. The 'China virus' campaign demonstrated Trump's willingness to endanger American citizens through racist scapegoating while using international tensions to cover for domestic policy failures.

title: Ivana Trump Physical and Sexual Abuse During Marriage
description_short: Ivana Trump Physical and Sexual Abuse During Marriage
description_medium: Ivana Trump’s 1990 divorce deposition included an account of a sexual encounter with Donald Trump that she described as rape. A 1993 clarification said she did not intend the word in a literal or criminal sense, and she said in 2015 that the allegation was “without merit.” Trump denied it. The available sources preserve these conflicting public statements, so the allegation should not be presented as an adjudicated fact.
description_long: Donald Trump physically and sexually assaulted his wife Ivana Trump during their marriage, with court deposition testimony describing violent rape after painful scalp surgery where Trump pulled out Ivana's hair in rage and forced sexual intercourse while she pleaded for him to stop, demonstrating escalating domestic violence and sexual assault within intimate relationship. The systematic spousal abuse included pattern of physical violence and sexual assault that Ivana described in sworn testimony as 'rape' during divorce proceedings, though she later recanted under pressure from confidentiality agreement that required Trump's permission for any public statements about their marriage. The domestic violence escalated during Trump's affair with Marla Maples, with physical and sexual abuse occurring during period when Trump was publicly humiliating Ivana through tabloid coverage while conducting extramarital relationship that violated marriage vows and family stability. Trump's spousal abuse violated criminal law and constitutional protections by using physical violence and sexual coercion within marriage while creating traumatic environment that included both physical assault and psychological abuse designed to control and terrorize intimate partner. The marital rape occurred during era when spousal rape was illegal in New York State, with Ivana's testimony providing detailed account of violent sexual assault that constituted criminal behavior masked by marriage relationship and later suppressed through legal settlements requiring victim silence. The domestic violence established Trump's foundational approach to intimate relationships and women's autonomy, demonstrating systematic willingness to use physical violence and sexual assault to control partners while using legal mechanisms to suppress victim testimony and accountability for criminal abuse within marriage.

title: Criminal Penalties for Teachers and School Librarians - Educator Imprisonment and Sex Offender Registration
description_short: Criminal Penalties for Teachers and School Librarians - Educator Imprisonment and Sex Offender Registration
description_medium: This entry concerns claims that teachers and school librarians could face criminal penalties for providing certain educational materials. The supplied long description attributes the penalties to January 2025 policy changes and Project 2025 rhetoric. The linked sources could not be retrieved in this pass, and the source list identifies no enacted statute or jurisdiction for the stated prison and registration penalties. Their legal status needs confirmation before those claims can be treated as implemented policy.
description_long: Donald Trump implemented Project 2025's criminalization of educators by establishing felony penalties including up to 2½ years imprisonment and $10,000 fines for teachers and school librarians who provided materials deemed 'obscene' or 'harmful' while stripping away 'educational purposes' defenses that had protected classroom instruction and library services from criminal prosecution. The systematic educator targeting represented Trump's strategy to transform teaching and library science from protected professions into criminal activities vulnerable to prosecution, with Heritage Foundation President Kevin Roberts calling for treating librarians as 'criminals' who should face 'stoned to death' threats for maintaining diverse book collections. The teacher criminalization included requiring 'public catalogs' of all school library materials while creating complaint systems that enabled political groups to trigger criminal investigations against educators who refused to remove books addressing LGBTQ+ topics, racial history, or reproductive health from classroom and library collections. Trump's educator persecution violated First Amendment academic freedom protections by threatening imprisonment for professional judgment about age-appropriate educational materials, creating 'chilling effect' where teachers and librarians self-censored rather than risk felony convictions for maintaining inclusive learning environments. The criminal penalty system created what education advocates called 'dangerous' conditions where librarians faced death threats and professional destruction for providing constitutionally protected educational resources, while legal systems treated classroom instruction and library services as potential criminal activity subject to prosecution rather than professional educational practice. The teacher and librarian criminalization represented Project 2025's vision of education controlled by political ideology rather than professional expertise, transforming schools from centers of learning into surveillance systems where educators faced imprisonment for maintaining diverse, inclusive, and intellectually comprehensive educational resources that acknowledged America's diversity and complexity.
